  - the ranking can flip between A and B: a skived or hinged fold concentrates the bend (higher strain in a free fold) but is thinner at the stack (lower strain around it).
  - strains within one thickness of the fold centre or of the start of the bend are excluded (constraint effects).
  - not modelled: permanent set, creep, finish-film cracking, glue-line shear, stitching, friction, and anything that changes with age.

results.title: Gussets
results.what: V, S and W pleats at several openings: the strain follows the fold angle.
results.output:
gusset (accordion pleat): shell 1.2 mm, E = 72 MPa (supply your own: strain does not depend on it, moment does)
crease groove: flesh side skived to 0.5 x t over 2 mm with 1.5 mm tapers (an assumption you vary). Free fold, 15 mm legs, plane strain, layers bonded.
A pleat is two opposed folds (an S). Fold 1 has the grain outside (grain in tension); fold 2 is its mirror, grain inside (grain in compression).
Fold angle 180 = pleat collapsed, smaller = opened. Moment is per mm of width: it is what the pleat pushes back with.
'grain' = the grain face of the shell; 'back' = the opposite face of the whole layup (the flesh side of a single leather, the lining of a lined one).

layup: plain
   fold  opened   moment    crease  central |  fold 1 grain   fold 1 back |  fold 2 grain   fold 2 back |  legs
  angle      by  N mm/mm    radius     6 mm |     (tension)      (compr.) |      (compr.)     (tension) | clear
    180      0%     1.19    9.7 mm      20% |          6.5%         -6.1% |         -6.1%          6.5% |   yes
    135     38%     0.89   12.9 mm      20% |          4.8%         -4.6% |         -4.6%          4.8% |   yes
     90     71%     0.60   19.4 mm      20% |          3.2%         -3.1% |         -3.1%          3.2% |   yes
     45     92%     0.30   38.8 mm      20% |          1.6%         -1.6% |         -1.6%          1.6% |   yes
  strain swing of the grain face between 180 and 90 deg: fold 1 3.3 points, fold 2 3.0 points (per open/close cycle)

   fold  opened   moment    crease  central |  fold 1 grain   fold 1 back |  fold 2 grain   fold 2 back |  legs
  angle      by  N mm/mm    radius     6 mm |     (tension)      (compr.) |      (compr.)     (tension) | clear
    180      0%     0.70    2.0 mm      53% |         16.0%        -13.7% |        -14.0%         16.0% |   yes
    135     38%     0.52    2.7 mm      53% |         11.8%        -10.5% |        -10.6%         11.8% |   yes

     45     92%     0.18    8.1 mm      53% |          3.8%         -3.6% |         -3.7%          3.8% |   yes
  strain swing of the grain face between 180 and 90 deg: fold 1 8.3 points, fold 2 6.7 points (per open/close cycle)

layup: grooved+lined
   fold  opened   moment    crease  central |  fold 1 grain   fold 1 back |  fold 2 grain   fold 2 back |  legs
  angle      by  N mm/mm    radius     6 mm |     (tension)      (compr.) |      (compr.)     (tension) | clear
    180      0%     2.58    3.3 mm      39% |         15.5%        -14.3% |        -13.7%         16.3% |   yes
    135     38%     1.95    4.4 mm      39% |         11.4%        -10.9% |        -10.4%         12.0% |   yes
     90     71%     1.31    6.7 mm      38% |          7.5%         -7.3% |         -7.1%          7.8% |   yes
     45     92%     0.66   13.4 mm      38% |          3.7%         -3.7% |         -3.6%          3.9% |   yes
  strain swing of the grain face between 180 and 90 deg: fold 1 8.0 points, fold 2 6.7 points (per open/close cycle)

KINDS OF GUSSET (all built from the two folds above)
  kind                                    creases  how it is simulated
  V gusset (one fold)                           1  one crease; fold 1 (grain out) or fold 2 (grain in) depending on which way it is folded
  S / Z accordion (two opposed folds)           2  fold 1 and fold 2 of `walletsim gusset`
  W / M accordion (three folds)                 3  the same two folds, one of them twice: each crease behaves as in the S
  n-fold zigzag                                 n  ceil(n/2) creases like fold 1 and floor(n/2) like fold 2
  round (U) gusset                              0  no crease: the strip wraps the contents; use `fold-styles --radius` with half the depth
  box gusset / flat spine                       0  two corners and a flat wall: `walletsim box-spine`
  'opened by' = how far the gusset has opened, as a fraction of its unfolded length: length x cos(fold angle / 2). For a zigzag of equal segments this is
  independent of the number of creases, so more creases do NOT lower the strain per crease at a given opening; they put the same strain on more creases.

NOTES
  - crease radius = radius of the neutral fibre at the fold centre as the FEM found it. A pleat is normally pressed into a sharper crease, which this elastic model cannot do
    (no permanent set), so real creases are tighter and more strained than the groove alone gives.
  - 'legs clear' = the inner face stays on its own side of the symmetry plane; contact between the two legs and with the contents is not modelled.
  - the strain swing, not the peak, is what repeats each time the pleat opens and closes. How often that happens per use is not known here.
  - not modelled: permanent set, creep, finish cracking, glue-line shear, stitching of the pleat edges, friction, ageing.

results.title: Box spine
results.what: A box-shaped spine with a flat wall, compared with the round spine.
results.output:
box-shaped spine: plain layup, shell 1.2 mm, E = 72 MPa; stack half thickness 1.9 mm (= 5.0 cards of 0.76 mm). Wrap load case, plane strain, layers bonded.
The end of the stack goes from a half-round (corner radius = half thickness) to a flat wall with two corners of smaller radius.

   corner  flat wall |  tension face at the corner  |  compression  stand-off
   radius     height |    loose     taut     limit |  face (taut)  loose, mm
   1.90 mm      round |    16.9%    17.9%     24.0% |       -15.6%       0.89
   1.50 mm     0.8 mm |    17.7%    18.8%     28.6% |       -16.0%       0.71
   1.00 mm     1.8 mm |    18.8%    19.8%     37.5% |       -16.6%       0.72
   0.50 mm     2.8 mm |    20.1%    21.1%     54.5% |       -17.5%       0.61

  limit = the leather follows the corner exactly (closed form, no solver).

NOTES
  - a square corner is not followed: the leather bridges it (stand-off), so the strain stays far below the limit. That is partly the model's elastic
    leather; a real corner is pressed and set, and would be tighter.
  - the flat wall is straight, so it carries no strain of its own; only the two corners do.
  - no closing moment is reported: the solver measures it at the fold centre, which on a box is the middle of the flat wall and says nothing about the corners,
    so it cannot be compared with the round spine's.
  - the stack is a rigid, frictionless block; not modelled: permanent set, creep, finish cracking, stitching, friction, ageing.

results.title: Turned edge
results.what: The 180 degree turn of a turned edge for several skive depths (closed form).
results.output:
turned edge, the 180 deg turn: 1.2 mm leather folded around a core (glue line, tape, or the other leg); kinematic strain t_turn / (2R + t_turn), R = core / 2

   skive  leather at   core   R/t  tension face    thickness that would give 20 %
   ratio    the turn   [mm]         (kinematic)                      at this core
    1.00     1.20 mm   0.60  0.25           67%                        0.150 mm
    1.00     1.20 mm   0.30  0.12           80%                        0.075 mm
    1.00     1.20 mm   0.10  0.04           92%                        0.025 mm
    0.50     0.60 mm   0.60  0.50           50%                        0.150 mm
    0.50     0.60 mm   0.30  0.25           67%                        0.075 mm
    0.50     0.60 mm   0.10  0.08           86%                        0.025 mm
    0.35     0.42 mm   0.60  0.71           41%                        0.150 mm
    0.35     0.42 mm   0.30  0.36           58%                        0.075 mm
    0.35     0.42 mm   0.10  0.12           81%                        0.025 mm
    0.25     0.30 mm   0.60  1.00           33%                        0.150 mm
    0.25     0.30 mm   0.30  0.50           50%                        0.075 mm
    0.25     0.30 mm   0.10  0.17           75%                        0.025 mm

NOTES
  - every row is far above the 20 % screening threshold (33 % to 92 %). Strains like these are not elastic, so a real turn must rely on
    permanent deformation, thinning and the glue. This model has none of those (no permanent set), so it cannot say whether a given turn survives.
  - what it does say is how much skiving buys: the kinematic strain falls as the leather at the turn gets thinner, and the last column is the thickness
    that would bring a turn around that core down to the screening threshold.
  - the hem as a double layer where the spine fold crosses it IS simulated: see the 'turned edge' row of `walletsim fold-styles`.
  - an elastic FEM of this turn was tried and rejected: around a 0.3-0.6 mm core the leather bridges the gap (strain 10-22 % against 41-80 % kinematic),
    because nothing in the model presses and glues it down.

                               [mm]                                                                  vs bifold     [N mm/mm]
  bifold                 1      8.5                      spine   14.1%   15.2%         1.00x to      1.000x          2.79
  trifold                2      9.7           inner fold (M|R)   18.3%   19.5%         2.12x to     20.355x          6.04
  z-fold (3 panels)      2      9.7 fold 1 (grain out) +1 tied   18.3%   19.5%         2.12x to     20.355x          6.95

NOTES
  - tension-face strain >= 20 % (screening threshold, not a failure criterion; the neo-Hookean model is unvalidated there): z-fold (4 panels)
  - folds are evaluated one at a time with the stack each wraps; their interaction, the pockets and card-slot edges, and the wallet's 3D shape are not modelled.
  - a fold's amplitude is closed -> flat; wallets are opened part-way in real use, and sit closed most of the time (creep and set, not modelled).
  - grain-in folds (z-fold) have the grain in compression and the back face in tension; the tension face is what is ranked.
  - the damage rates are relative and uncalibrated, with no leather-specific exponent; they say which wallet is gentler, not how long anything lasts.
